subject: Post-call: private deployment constraints & data-handling follow-ups
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@clearbridgehealth.com>, ClearBridge Ops <ops@clearbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — Private deployment & PII controls (next steps)

Thanks again for the call today, Amit — good to connect. Quick recap and open items we agreed to follow up on: 

Summary
- You're evaluating a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood for clinical summarization and search. Primary constraints: PII/PHI residency in customer VPC, restricted egress, 3rd-party telemetry, and retention windows driven by compliance.

Open/Action items (from Redwood)
- Provide a first-pass VPC data-flow diagram and recommended network boundary/egress controls (Jonas).
- Call out specific controls for PII-at-rest and KMS/HSM integration, and evidence artifacts for SOC 2/ISO (Neha).
- Confirm what ClearBridge can accept for short-term log retention and DSAR handling (Amit).
- Share procurement contact and high-level timing for Dedicated/Private SOW (Amit — you mentioned procurement).

Attachments referenced: none in this email — we'll attach the data-flow draft in the next note.

As next steps we propose: Jonas will send the VPC diagram + recommended guardrails by COB Mon 23 Nov. Neha will follow with compliance checklist and required artifacts by Tue 24 Nov. Can you confirm the following from your side so we can make the diagram concrete?

Short questions for CBH
1) Do you require full air-gapped (no outbound internet) operation for PHI workloads, or is controlled egress to specific endpoints allowed?
2) Minimum/maximum retention windows for logs vs. derived records (e.g., summaries) — you mentioned legal may need 7 years for records, but curious about operational logs.
3) CIDR ranges or peering constraints we should model.

If a quick 30-min follow-up helps to lock those details, happy to schedule for next week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0123

From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@clearbridgehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, ClearBridge Ops <ops@clearbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Private deployment & PII controls (next steps)

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 

1) Airgap vs controlled egress: For PHI workloads we prefer no general internet egress. Controlled, allow-listed egress to a small set of vendor endpoints (e.g., telemetry or update services) is acceptable if traffic is forced through an egress proxy that we control. We need to see the exact endpoints before approving.

2) Retention windows: Legal requires retention of clinical records (derived summaries) up to 7 years. Operational logs (access logs, request logs) we prefer max 90 days by default, but we can extend under retention policies or legal hold.

3) CIDR/peering: We'll share a sanitized CIDR block and peering owner next week — putting point procurement@clearbridgehealth.com on copy for SOW/timing.

Also: we need to ensure no raw audio or source PHI leaves our VPC. Output summaries can be optionally exported to a REDACTED bucket; we'll clarify which modules are allowed to export.

If you can provide the VPC diagram with egress controls and a list of endpoints you require for updates/metrics, we can review with Infra next week and flag anything that needs changes.

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Sr. Product Manager, Data Platforms
ClearBridge Health
amit.shah@clearbridgehealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@clearbridgehealth.com>, ClearBridge Ops <ops@clearbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: VPC data-flow draft & recommended egress/controls (CBH)

Amit — attaching a first-pass VPC data-flow and controls doc for the PHI workload. High-level notes first, then the attachment and requested confirmations.

Attachment: CBH_vpc_dataflow_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 412KB)
Also attached: redwood-private-reqs-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB)

High-level approach - Private deployment model: Redwood runtime (in customer VPC) + optional Redwood control plane endpoints that can be configured over private peering or customer-managed VPN. If you require full air-gap, control plane traffic can be disabled and updates shipped through an approved jump host process.

Network boundaries & egress recommendations
- Recommended: Block all outbound Internet from model worker subnets by default. Allow egress only via a dedicated Egress NAT/proxy subnets that are customer-managed and go through an outbound inspection stack.
- Allow-listed outbound hosts: (placeholder, please confirm) api.redwood-updates.redwood.com (updates), telemetry.redwood-internal.redwood.com (optional, can be disabled), docker-registries (optional, on-prem mirroring recommended).
- mTLS for any control-plane connections. Public endpoints should only be allowed if routed through the customer's egress proxy.

PII handling & storage
- All raw inputs (PHI) remain inside customer subnets (no automatic replication).
- Persistent artifacts: derived summaries — can be written to customer-managed S3-compatible bucket with customer KMS keys.
- KV cache and swap on worker nodes must be ephemeral and encrypted at rest (LUKS) with keys managed by customer KMS or HSM.

Logging & retention
- Application-level request logs: configurable retention; default 90 days. We can support shorter retention by policy.
- Audit logs (who accessed what): retained 1 year by default; extendable to meet your compliance needs.
- Option for per-tenant log scrubbing/masking prior to any telemetry leaving VPC.

Operational notes / blockers for diagram finalization
- Please confirm whether the control plane will be allowed private peering to your VPC, or you require an entirely customer-managed control plane (air-gapped).
- Confirm exact CIDR ranges and egress FQDNs you will allow so we can populate the diagram.

Next steps
1) Action (Jonas): Share updated diagram after we get CIDR + allowed egress list (tentative Tue/Wed).
2) Action (Neha): Send the compliance evidence checklist (SOC 2 artifacts, encryption proofs) by Tue 24 Nov.
3) Action (Amit): Introduce procurement so we can start SOW + timeline.

If it helps, we can set a short tech deep-dive with your infra team Thurs or Fri next week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@clearbridgehealth.com>, ClearBridge Ops <ops@clearbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Compliance artifacts & minimum security checklist for Private deployment (CBH)

Amit — following up with the minimum evidence set and a few clarifying questions. I attached a spreadsheet with the evidence items we can provide.

Key requirements we can meet and items we need from you
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; data at rest encrypted with customer-managed KMS/HSM recommended. We support Bring-Your-Own-KMS (BYOK) for Redwood Private.
- Key management: Customer-managed keys (rotate per your policy). HSM-backed keys are supported for highest assurance.
- Audit & access logs: We can stream audit logs to a customer-managed log sink (S3/Cloud Storage) under your account. We recommend retention = 1 year default; configurable.
- DSAR & deletion: We support record-level deletion & masking if you provide identifiers. For legal hold, we can quarantine objects and export evidence.
- Subprocessors: If you use the hosted control plane, Redwood uses a small set of subprocessors (listed in the attached sheet). If you prohibit subprocessors, we can discuss an entirely customer-managed control plane option.

Questions for CBH
1) Does Legal require any specific certifications for 3rd-party subprocessors beyond SOC 2 (e.g., HITRUST)?
2) Confirm whether you will allow streaming of non-identifiable telemetry (p50 latency, error rates) to Redwood for support and cost-optimization. We can disable telemetry if required.
3) For audit: provide the retention window you need for access logs vs. request logs; we will map those to config options.

Deliverables schedule
- Neha: compliance evidence spreadsheet (attached) — sent now.
- Jonas: updated diagram after CIDRs received.
- Vanessa: will coordinate scheduling and procurement introduction.

Attachment: redwood-private-reqs-checklist.xlsx (see row-level items)

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Private deployment & PII controls (next steps)

Thanks all — this is very helpful. Confirmations and next steps from ClearBridge: 

- We will not permit general internet egress from PHI worker subnets. Controlled egress via a customer-managed egress proxy is acceptable for updates, subject to allow-listing.
- Retention: operational logs 90 days; derived clinical records 7 years. Audit logs retention request: 3 years. Legal will provide formal retention table to Vanessa early next week.
- Subprocessor constraints: our legal team prefers no new subprocessors without review. If you propose any hosted control-plane subprocessors, we will need their SOC 2 reports.

Procurement contact: procurement@clearbridgehealth.com (please include SOW, high-level pricing, and expected timeline). Proposed timeline: 6–8 weeks from SOW signature to a first Private deployment in staging.

Jonas — we can provide sanitized CIDR ranges and a point-of-contact for the infra deep-dive: ops@clearbridgehealth.com. Please include any short pre-read (diagram + list of endpoints) and we'll book a 60-min slot next week.

Vanessa — please connect procurement and share an initial SOW draft and rough pricing bands so procurement can triage.

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Sr. Product Manager, Data Platforms
ClearBridge Health
